claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let's work through the eligibility for Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask a follow-up question about his education or training status.

Is Alex currently in full-time education (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or equivalent) or on an approved training course? Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's actually just left school recently. He signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

When Alex registered with the local careers service, was this through an approved body for education, employment, or training (such as Careers Wales, a local authority service, or similar organisation)? And is he currently not in a job, education, or training (sometimes referred to as NEET)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - he registered with the local careers service, and he's not working or in education or training at the moment. He's just trying to work out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is really helpful.

One more question: How recently did Alex leave school? Specifically, was it within the last 20 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was fairly recent - within the last few months, so yes, within the last 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I have just one more question: Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care, and does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**Alex (age 16)** ✅ Eligible

Alex qualifies because:
- He is 16 years old
- He left school recently (within the last 20 weeks)
- He has registered with an approved careers service
- He is not currently working, in education, or training
- He lives with you and you are responsible for his care

**Important to note:** This eligibility extends for up to 20 weeks from when Alex left education, as long as he remains registered with the careers service and doesn't start work, education, or training. If his situation changes (for example, if he starts a job or begins a course), you would need to inform the Child Benefit Office.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old and has recently left school (within the last 20 weeks). Although he is not currently in full-time education or training, he has registered with an approved careers service and is not currently employed, in education, or training. Under Child Benefit rules, you can continue to claim for a child aged 16-17 who has left education or training, provided they have registered with an approved careers service or similar body and are not in work, education, or training - and this continues for up to 20 weeks after leaving education. Since Alex meets all these criteria and lives with you while you are responsible for his care, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.
